info.title: ratchet - the two-level roadmap runner.
info.description: Ratchet — a two-level roadmap runner that drives a coding agent through a roadmap phase by phase, gating on verdicts and metering cost per step.

commands.name: codex-stop-hook
commands.description: the Codex Stop-hook entrypoint: run the rollout's injected gate for an armed step and answer on stdout. Registered by the tool in .codex/hooks.json on a Codex rollout; not meant to be typed

options.name: --manifest
options.description: manifest file (default: Plans/rollouts.json)

options.name: --rollout
options.description: rollout entry (default: the sole entry, if unambiguous)

options.name: --roadmap
options.description: roadmap file the run drives (optional: the rollout's manifest 'roadmap' key supplies it; this flag overrides it for one run)

options.name: --repo-root
options.description: repository root (default: .)

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: print the resolved plan and exit; no claude, no git (a Reap-bound rollout is read, never written)

options.name: --report
options.description: build the metering report from the persisted store and exit; no claude, no git

options.name: --bill
options.description: build the per-client billing report under the manifest commercial model and exit; no claude, no git

options.name: --reconcile
options.description: reconcile the measured estimate against the Usage & Cost API billed figure and exit; no claude, no git

options.name: --report-out
options.description: directory the report/billing/reconciliation artifacts are written to (default: .ratchet/)

options.name: --from
options.description: start at this roadmap phase, skipping earlier (already-closed) phases (alias: --start-phase)

options.name: --single-phase
options.description: stop after the first in-scope phase closes (don't chain on); review it, then re-run with --from <next> (default off: chain to the end of the roadmap, one stacked branch per phase, merged and tagged once at the end)

options.name: --stop-file
options.description: request a clean stop between rungs by creating this file; the run stops at the next rung boundary (resumable) and deletes it

options.name: --skip-readiness-check
options.description: skip the plugin-enabled preflight (escape hatch for false negatives)

options.name: --skip-base-ancestry-check
options.description: skip the phase-boundary check that a phase branch's base already contains the previous phase's branch (escape hatch, e.g. a squash-merged previous phase)

options.name: --claude-path
options.description: explicit claude launcher path (overrides PATH; also via RATCHET_CLAUDE)

options.name: --model
options.description: run every role-step of this session on this Claude model (alias or full id, passed verbatim to claude --model); overrides the manifest's model/models

options.name: --provider
options.description: run every role-step of this session against this manifest 'providers' entry, overriding the rollout's own provider

options.name: --no-provider
options.description: run on the ambient Anthropic endpoint, suppressing the rollout's provider (cannot be combined with --provider)

options.name: --harness
options.description: init only: the harness the new rollout's role-steps run under (claude, the default, or codex); recorded in the entry the init session authors and read from the manifest thereafter - no other verb accepts it

options.name: --stop-entry
options.description: import only: stop the running Reap entry this D-5 reference names (as the preflight, doctor and import lines print it) at the finish given by --finished-at; one entry per invocation

options.name: --finished-at
options.description: import only, with --stop-entry: the finish, in Reap's own wall-clock form yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss (the zone the entry's start was written in); must be after the entry's start

options.name: --quiet
options.description: suppress per-step narration and lifecycle chatter (warnings/failures still shown)

options.name: --verbose
options.description: print rolled-up listings in full (every dirty path, not directory counts), and echo each role-step child's own stderr live as it arrives

options.name: --no-color
options.description: disable ANSI colour/styling (also honoured via the NO_COLOR environment variable)

options.name: --no-pulse
options.description: disable the live step activity line (on by default on a real terminal; already off when redirected, NO_COLOR, --no-color or --quiet)

options.name: --pr-review
options.description: after each phase closes, open a PR, review it in a fresh session, and on a clean verdict auto-merge (opt-in; default off; also via manifest prReview)

options.name: --max-pr-iterations
options.description: PR review↔remediate cap (default: 3)

options.name: --allow-dirty
options.description: bypass the clean-tree preflight

options.name: --retry-count
options.description: transient-failure retries (default: 2)

options.name: --retry-delay-seconds
options.description: base backoff delay (default: 20)

options.name: --stall-timeout-minutes
options.description: cancel an attempt after this long with NO stream activity (default: 15; 0 = off) - a still-emitting session is never cancelled

options.name: --result-timeout-minutes
options.description: optional absolute per-attempt ceiling, firing even while the session is active (default: 0 = off)

options.name: --style-sample
options.description: render one example of every element of the terminal design and exit; no claude, no git, no repository (mode: catalogue|run|both, default both)

options.name: --style-sample-capabilities
options.description: render the sample at all four colour x box-drawing combinations, not just this terminal's

options.name: --style-sample-width
options.description: lay the sample out at this width instead of the detected one (e.g. 80)

options.name: --no-events
options.description: do not write the run-events observability log (on by default)

options.name: --version
options.description: print the tool version and exit

options.name: --help
options.description:
show this help
Relative --manifest, --roadmap, --report-out, and --stop-file paths resolve against
--repo-root; absolute paths are used verbatim.
Graceful stop: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+Break, SIGTERM, a console-window close/logoff, or creating
the --stop-file all stop the run cleanly at the next rung boundary, resumable. A forced
kill (taskkill /F) is not survivable; the interrupted rung is re-driven on the next run.
Resume is automatic: re-run the same command and the runner continues from the
recorded state log (.ratchet/<rollout>.events.jsonl).
Observability: the run publishes structured events (run and role-step lifecycle, tool
calls, per-session cost, gate verdicts, iterations, checkpoints) to
.ratchet/<rollout>.run-events.jsonl as they happen. Tail it live with
`Get-Content -Wait .ratchet/<rollout>.run-events.jsonl`. It is a record, never a
control input - a failing events log warns once and the run carries on unchanged.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: diagnose the rollout's last recorded halt in one agent session over the structured logs (.ratchet/<rollout>.*.jsonl); proposes a remedy, never applies one

commands.name: import
commands.description: import the repository's .ratchet/ metering and state logs into Reap for every bound rollout (or the one named) as the same tasks, entries and expenses a live run lands; --dry-run reports what it would write and reads Reap only

commands.name: init
commands.description: examine the repo + roadmap in one agent session and author/extend the manifest (Plans/rollouts.json)

commands.name: reap
commands.description: prepare a rollout for Reap: read the Reap settings in its manifest entry and create in Reap whatever is missing (client, project, task types, the recording person's assignment); --dry-run reports what it would create and reads Reap only

commands.name: triage
commands.description: start a triage cycle: run the manifest's triage.listCommand and write the batch into a dated folder under the rollout's plans directory; run again, assess the drawn batch in one agent session into the decision document; run again, check the decision document's gate and report which entries still need a settled stamp; once the gate passes, compose the rollout in one agent session, add it to the manifest and print the command that runs it (triage never starts it); run again after the rollout has finished a run, close the cycle in one agent session and write its close report, whose status changes go to the tracker through triage.updateCommand when the manifest sets one, or else you apply them by hand
